key_insight: GaDiT generates disordered atomic structures and enables interpretable inverse design toward target properties, including beyond training-distribution ranges.
engineering_relevance: The framework could accelerate exploration of amorphous materials by linking atomic disorder to desired properties and preparation conditions.
method: Combines dynamic periodic graphs with a diffusion transformer.
Uses masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution.
Applies conditioned atomic response mapping to identify influential structural descriptors and local environments.
evidence_signal: Across 2D amorphous carbon and 3D amorphous silicon and silica, the abstract reports high-quality generation and sampling two orders of magnitude faster than existing corrector-based approaches.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish physical validation or generalization beyond the demonstrated material systems.
paper_title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
